author: cometkim
body:
Compiler JS bundles are uploaded into a Cloudflare R2 bucket.

https://github.com/rescript-lang/rescript/pull/7472

Serving resources from the same-origin removes CORS preflight when visiting the playground and prevents charges for R2 reads.

I made the `sync-bundles` script to download all resources from the bucket.

And we have two options:

1. Commit resources to git
   - Only new versions can be additionally downloaded.
   - The repo will get significant bloat.
2. Don't commit resources to git
   - For developers, they need to sync it at least once.
   - The sync must be run per deployment, which will significantly slow down.

Option 2 is not feasible for Vercel deployments, but for Cloudflare Pages.

Alternatively, we can run a [custom deployment with GitHub Actions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/ci-cd/external-cicd/github-actions/) (When we use Cloudflare Workers instead of Pages). Option 2 + `@actions/cache` would be the best.

author: tarepan
body:
## 内容
`UtteranceLabel.pauses` を削除するリファクタリングを提案します。  

`UtteranceLabel` はテキスト解析部分の橋渡しを担うクラスであり、値を変換しコンテナとして収納している。
調査の結果、`.pauses` 属性がテストのみで利用され、ENGINE 本体のコードで利用されていないことがわかった。  
`.pauses` は `UtteranceLabel.labels()` で利用されており、一見すると ENGINE 本体で利用されている。しかし `.labels()` はテスト用のユーティリティメソッドであるため、`.pauses` は実態としてテストでのみ利用されている。  
そしてこのテストでは「`.pauses` はちゃんと機能しているか」を確かめており、そのために `.labels()` 内で `.pauses` が使われている。つまり「実利用されていない`.pauses` 属性のテストのために、`.pauses` 属性が使われている」状態にある。  
であれば削除により処理を単純化するほうが望ましい。  

このような背景から、`UtteranceLabel.pauses` を削除するリファクタリングを提案します。  

## 関連 Issue
part of #1686

This PR implements a robust, production-ready integration with the Stripe Customer Billing Portal, along with several improvements to subscription management and authentication. Key changes include:
Stripe Billing Portal:
Adds a secure Billing link in the user dropdown that redirects authenticated users to the Stripe Customer Portal for managing their subscription (upgrade, cancel, payment methods, etc.).
Robust Authentication:
Ensures users are authenticated using both Supabase session and secure cookie fallback, improving reliability in both local and production environments.
RLS-Safe Subscription Lookup:
Uses the Supabase admin client for server-side subscription queries, bypassing Row Level Security (RLS) and ensuring accurate results.
Environment-Aware Return URL:
The Stripe portal’s “Return to my site” button now correctly redirects users to the appropriate dashboard in both local and production environments.
Extensive Debugging & Logging:
Adds helpful debug logs for easier troubleshooting and environment verification.
Tested:
Works in both local development and production environments
Handles all authentication and subscription edge cases
Stripe portal integration is fully functional in test mode

author: subtlegradient
body:
This pull request introduces a migration to a Nix-based development environment, replacing previous shell scripts and configurations. Key changes include adding a `flake.nix` file for environment management, updating `package.json` scripts and dependencies, and removing legacy scripts and tools.

### Migration to Nix-based Environment:
* Added `.envrc` to integrate with `direnv`, setting up environment variables and watching `flake.nix` and `flake.lock` for updates.
* Introduced `flake.nix` to define the development environment using Nix, including dependencies like `jq`, `bun`, `nodejs_24`, and `ripgrep`.

### Updates to `package.json`:
* Updated the `sh` script to use `nix develop` instead of `nix-shell`.
* Bumped versions of `prettier`, `turbo`, `typescript`, and `bun` in `devDependencies`.
* Removed the `tools` configuration section, previously used for tool version checks and management.

### Removal of Legacy Scripts:
* Deleted `sh/pod.sh`, which configured and managed a Podman machine.
* Removed `sh/sh.sh`, which handled tool validation and environment setup.
* Removed `shell.nix`, which was used for managing the development environment before migrating to flakes.

author: ben-westphal
body:
* Added new rule allowing the user to check environment variables for quotes that would be included in the string.

Eg: It will provide a warning for the following: `REALLY_COOL_ENVIRONMENT: "super-cool-environment"` as the double quotes will end up included in the string.
This often happens when someone copy pastes the variable from another environment which will parse the quoting as expected.
It can be turned on and off in your config file with the value `NoQuotedEnvRule: boolean`

* Added a config file

This config file can be added to your .buildkite directory to turn specific rules on and off, as well as add in external environment variables that may be injected from outside your pipeline.

author: alex-au1
body:
- Allow more granularity control for the user on how to control the algorithm for determining what files to download. Download modes can be found at the link below:
https://anime-game-remap.readthedocs.io/en/latest/commandOpts.html#download-modes

- Editted texture files require the following information as their candidate key:
   - Mod To Fix
   - Mod Object
   - Texture Name
   - File Name

  `Mod To Fix` and `Mod Object` are already in the original name of the editted texture, but we do not have the last 2 pieces of info. To not clutter up the file name to be too long, `Texture Name` and `File Name` is encoded in a base 64 MD5 encoding that has a integer range from -65536 to 65536. Repeated hashes are dealt using [chaining](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/separate-chaining-collision-handling-technique-in-hashing/). So most of the time, we only use 3 characters to encode some info.

author: abiteman
body:
Fixes #32 

## Issue
Fixed issue #32 where editing a transaction would throw a `ReferenceError: currentTransactionType is not defined` error. This occurred when trying to edit a transaction after previously editing another transaction.

## Changes Made
- Moved all global variable declarations to the top of the file for better organization and initialization
- Consolidated scattered variable declarations into a single global variables section
- Ensured `currentTransactionType` is properly initialized before any function usage
- Removed duplicate declarations that were scattered throughout the file

## Technical Details
The issue was caused by the `currentTransactionType` variable being declared in the middle of the file, which could lead to reference errors if the code execution path didn't reach that declaration before using the variable. By moving it to the top of the file with other global variables, we ensure it's always properly initialized before use.

## Testing
The fix has been tested by:
1. Editing an expense transaction
2. Editing an income transaction
3. Verifying that the transaction type remains correct during edits
4. Confirming no more reference errors occur

## Impact
This change improves the reliability of the transaction editing functionality and prevents potential type switching issues when editing different types of transactions in sequence.

This PR implements a decentralized supply chain risk management system using Clarity smart contracts. The system enables supply chain participants to verify entities, assess risks, monitor conditions, manage alerts, and track mitigation efforts.

## Components

### Entity Verification Contract
- Validates supply chain participants
- Allows registration and verification of entities
- Tracks verification status and history

### Risk Assessment Contract
- Identifies potential disruption factors
- Allows creation and assessment of risk factors
- Maps risks to specific entities

### Monitoring Contract
- Tracks conditions affecting the supply chain
- Defines thresholds for various monitoring parameters
- Records data points and detects threshold breaches

### Alert Management Contract
- Handles notification of potential issues
- Manages alert status and subscriptions
- Links alerts to monitors and entities

### Mitigation Tracking Contract
- Records actions to address risks
- Tracks mitigation plans and individual actions
- Monitors progress toward risk resolution

## Testing
- Comprehensive test suite using Vitest
- Tests individual contract functionality
- Includes end-to-end workflow testing

## Implementation Notes
- All contracts use a simple admin model for privileged operations
- Data is stored in maps with appropriate keys
- Status values are represented as uint constants
- Contracts are designed to work together in a cohesive system

body:
This codemod refactors SQL statements to be parameterized, rather than built by hand.

Without parameterization, developers must remember to escape string inputs using the rules for that column type and database. This usually results in bugs -- and sometimes vulnerabilities. Although we can't tell for sure if your code is actually exploitable, this change will make the code more robust in case the conditions which prevent exploitation today ever go away.

Our changes look something like this:

```diff
import sqlite3

name = input()
connection = sqlite3.connect("my_db.db")
cursor = connection.cursor()
- cursor.execute("SELECT * from USERS WHERE name ='" + name + "'")
+ cursor.execute("SELECT * from USERS WHERE name =?", (name, ))
```

author: burtonqin
body:
# Unsound API design in opt_bytes_to_ptr

The original `opt_bytes_to_ptr` function accepts a parameter of type `Option<T> where T: AsRef<[u8]>`. While this is flexible, it also allows owned types like `String` or `Vec<u8>` to be passed in. Since the function takes ownership of T, any owned data (like a `String`) will be dropped at the end of the function scope.

This results in undefined behavior, as the returned `*const c_char` pointer may point to memory that is already freed, leading to dangling pointers.

See the example below:
https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=a59bc55798c258040f5aa04c9e60c1b5

## Fix: Change to borrowed data
To resolve this, the function should accept a borrowed reference instead, such as:
The function no longer takes ownership of the data.
The returned pointer is guaranteed to be valid for at least as long as the input reference.

## Safety Note
It is the caller's responsibility to ensure the borrowed data outlives any use of the returned raw pointer. This is a standard requirement when interfacing with raw C-style APIs.

## Additional Changes
Added documentation to clarify the ownership and lifetime requirements of the input data and returned pointer.

body:
This codemod sandboxes all instances of [subprocess.run](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.run) and [subprocess.call](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.call) to offer protection against attack.

Left unchecked, `subprocess.run` and `subprocess.call` can execute any arbitrary system command. If an attacker can control part of the strings used as program paths or arguments, they could execute arbitrary programs, install malware, and anything else they could do if they had a shell open on the application host.

Our change introduces a sandbox which protects the application:

```diff
  import subprocess
+ from security import safe_command
  ...
- subprocess.run("echo 'hi'", shell=True)
+ safe_command.run(subprocess.run, "echo 'hi'", shell=True)
  ...
- subprocess.call(["ls", "-l"])
+ safe_command.call(subprocess.call, ["ls", "-l"])
```

The default `safe_command` restrictions applied are the following:
* **Prevent command chaining**. Many exploits work by injecting command separators and causing the shell to interpret a second, malicious command. The `safe_command` functions attempt to parse the given command, and throw a `SecurityException` if multiple commands are present.
* **Prevent arguments targeting sensitive files.** There is little reason for custom code to target sensitive system files like `/etc/passwd`, so the sandbox prevents arguments that point to these files that may be targets for exfiltration.

There are [more options for sandboxing](https://github.com/pixee/python-security/blob/main/src/security/safe_command/api.py#L5) if you are interested in locking down system commands even more.

## Dependency Updates

This codemod relies on an external dependency. We have automatically added this dependency to your project's `pyproject.toml` file. 

This library holds security tools for protecting Python API calls. 

There are a number of places where Python project dependencies can be expressed, including `setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, and `requirements.txt` files. If this change is incorrect, or if you are using another packaging system such as `poetry`, it may be necessary for you to manually add the dependency to the proper location in your project.

author: deweyjose
body:
Overview
This PR is a significant refactor and test enhancement for the graphqlcodegen-maven-plugin and related modules. The main goals are to decouple the code generation logic from Maven internals, improve testability, and ensure that the plugin's configuration surface is robustly mapped to the underlying DGS codegen library (see Netflix/dgs-codegen CodeGenConfig).
Key Changes
1. Decoupling and Refactoring
* Extracted CodegenExecutor: The core code generation logic is now in a new CodegenExecutor class, which operates on a CodegenConfigProvider interface. This makes the logic testable without Maven and enables easier future extension.
* Introduced CodegenConfigProvider: This interface abstracts all configuration needed for codegen, making it explicit and decoupled from Maven's @Parameter injection.
* Refactored DependencySchemaExtractor: Now works with a set of Maven Artifacts directly, not the MavenProject, further reducing Maven coupling.
* Renamed Properties → ParameterMap: To avoid confusion with java.util.Properties and clarify intent.
2. Test Coverage and Quality
* Comprehensive Unit Tests: Added CodegenExecutorTest and DependencySchemaExtractorTest to cover all major logic branches, including edge cases for schema path expansion, type mapping merging, and error handling.
* Integration Test: Added CodegenExecutorExecuteTest which runs a real codegen flow against test schemas and asserts on the generated output structure and content.
* Mockito and JUnit 5: Test dependencies and usage are now explicit and up-to-date.
3. Maven Plugin and Build Improvements
* Plugin POMs: Updated dependencies and plugin configurations for better test support and source generation.
* Build Helper Plugin: Ensures generated sources are added to the build.
* Kotlin and JavaPoet: Added as dependencies for parameter codegen and builder generation.
4. Parameter Mapping and Builder Generation
* BuilderCodegen Mojo: New Maven goal in graphqlcodegen-param-plugin that fetches the latest CodeGenConfig.kt from Netflix/dgs-codegen, parses its constructor, and generates a Java builder class. This ensures our plugin's config surface stays in sync with upstream.
* Tests for BuilderCodegen: Validates that parameter extraction and builder generation work as expected, using real and test resources.
5. General Cleanups
* Removed dead code and legacy classes (e.g., ParamCodegen.java).
* Improved logging and error messages throughout.
* Minor bugfixes (e.g., schema file extension handling).
Why This Matters
* Testability: The plugin logic can now be tested in isolation, with or without Maven, and is covered by both unit and integration tests.
* Maintainability: Decoupling from Maven internals and explicit config mapping makes future changes safer and easier.
* Correctness: The builder/codegen parameter mapping is now always aligned with the upstream DGS codegen library, reducing the risk of config drift.
* Extensibility: New features or config options can be added with minimal friction.
How to Review
* See CodegenExecutor.java and CodegenConfigProvider.java for the new abstraction.
* Review the new and updated tests for coverage and intent.
* See the new BuilderCodegen.java for how parameter mapping is kept in sync with upstream.
* All changes are backward compatible for plugin users, but the codebase is now much easier to reason about and extend.

# 🚀 Feature Enhancements and Refactoring

## Summary

This pull request introduces several enhancements and refactorings to improve the user experience and functionality of GitWise. The changes include:

- Enhanced pull request creation with improved error handling, title generation, and description generation
- Simplified and improved user flows for the `add` and `commit` commands
- Added changelog generation feature
- Refactored code for better organization and maintainability

## Enhancements

### Pull Requests

- Handle empty commit list and improve error handling
- Add pull request creation functionality
- Generate PR titles and enhance PR description generation
- Add `--no-group` flag to `commit` command
- Make labels and checklist opt-in for PR enhancements

### Changelog

- Add changelog generation command
- Enhance changelog generation with version parsing and comparison
- Add `--create-tag` option to changelog command

### CLI Commands

- Enhance `add` command UI and workflow with smart file preview, diff table, and selective staging
- Simplify `add` and `commit` command flows and prompts
- Add smart commit grouping option

## Refactoring

- Improve error handling and user experience when creating PRs
- Simplify command flows and improve overall user experience
- Extract LLM API call to separate function
- Simplify `generate_pr_description` function
- Update `get_commit_history` to compare against remote
- Organize code for better maintainability

## Documentation and Tests

- Add API documentation for GitWise
- Add contributing guidelines and code of conduct

- Add unit tests for `pr` command, helpers, and `commit` feature

- application deploys automatically on push using GitHub Actions

author: sofiaqsy
body:
## Corrección del Formato de Fechas en Compras

Este Pull Request soluciona el problema detectado con la visualización de fechas en la hoja de compras, donde las fechas se mostraban incorrectamente como números (por ejemplo, `45795.04447` en lugar de `2025-05-08 13:14`).

### Problema Identificado

Google Sheets convierte automáticamente los valores que identifica como fechas a un formato numérico interno, lo que causa problemas de visualización. Específicamente:
- Las fechas se muestran como números (ej. `45795.04447`)
- El formato es inconsistente entre diferentes registros
- Al exportar/importar datos, los formatos pueden perderse

### Solución Implementada

Se implementó una solución integral en tres niveles:

#### 1. Prevención en Nuevos Registros

- Nueva función `format_date_for_sheets` en `utils/helpers.py` que añade una comilla simple (`'`) al inicio de las fechas
- Actualización del handler de compras para aplicar el formato correcto antes de guardar

#### 2. Corrección Automática de Registros Existentes

- Actualización de `initialize_sheets()` para identificar y corregir fechas con formato incorrecto
- Se aplica al iniciar el bot, asegurando que las fechas estén siempre correctamente formateadas

#### 3. Herramienta de Mantenimiento

- Script `fix_date_formats.py` para corregir todas las fechas en todas las hojas como operación de mantenimiento
- Detecta automáticamente todas las columnas de fecha y aplica la corrección donde sea necesario

### Archivos Modificados

1. `utils/sheets.py`: Actualización del manejo de fechas en las funciones `append_data` y `update_cell`
2. `utils/helpers.py`: Nueva función `format_date_for_sheets` para estandarizar el formato
3. `handlers/compras.py`: Uso de la nueva función para formatear fechas antes de guardar
4. `fix_date_formats.py`: Nuevo script para corregir fechas existentes
5. `docs/DATE_FORMAT_FIX.md`: Documentación detallada del problema y la solución

### Beneficios

1. **Visualización correcta**: Las fechas se muestran en formato legible (`2025-05-08 13:14`) en lugar de números
2. **Consistencia**: Formato uniforme en todos los registros y operaciones
3. **Integridad de datos**: Al preservar el formato de texto, se evita la conversión automática
4. **Mantenibilidad**: Solución extensible a futuras columnas o datos que incluyan fechas

### Pruebas Realizadas

- Verificado el correcto funcionamiento del comando `/compra` con el nuevo formato de fechas
- Comprobada la corrección automática de fechas existentes
- Probado el script `fix_date_formats.py` en un entorno de prueba

### Capturas de pantalla

**Antes:**
![Imagen mostrando fechas como números](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12345678/imagen-problema.png)

**Después:**
Las fechas ahora se muestran correctamente como texto en formato YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.

author: ikawrakow
body:
There have been several crash reports (#398, #425) for large MoE models when using hybrid GPU/CPU inference. As I don't have the hardware to run such large models I'm not able to debug. But with help from @nux, who ran `llama-server` in the debugger on his computer and gave me a backtrace along with a few variables values (see [this](https://github.com/ikawrakow/ik_llama.cpp/issues/425#issuecomment-2888464768) and [this](https://github.com/ikawrakow/ik_llama.cpp/issues/425#issuecomment-2888500696), my hypothesis is that the problem is with the multi-add operation that I added to `ik_llama.cpp`.

I'm of course not sure if the hypothesis is correct as it is based on very scarce evidence. Hence I would appreciate if the people reporting a problem test this PR and let me know if it fixes the problem, so pinging @Panchovix, @ciprianveg, @pt13762104, @schynce, @p4s2wd

### Background

What is multi-add? In MoE models the contributions of the routed experts need to be added together. In mainline `llama.cpp` this is done via `N-1` consecutive `GGML_OP_ADD` operations, where `N` is the number of active experts. This is not a problem when `N` is small as in the early MoE models (e.g., Mixtral8x7 with 2 active experts). But more recent models such as DeepSeek-V3/R1 and Qwen3-235B-A22B have 8 active experts, so this means 7 additional graph nodes with 7 additional synchronization points, causing a non-negligible overhead. Hence, I added the multi-add operation, which adds `N` tensors in one go. The operation works fine if everything is done on one device. But it looks like things can go wrong when data needs to be copied between devices. I don't observe the problem when using the smaller siblings of these models (Qwen-22B-A3B and DeepSeek-Lite) in my setup with hybrid GPU/CPU inference, but looking at my implementation it appears there could be an issue. The PR reverts to the original implementation, so it will result in a small performance penalty (2-3% with the models I can run).

author: idraliski
body:
This pull request introduces a significant refactor to the shader system, consolidating vertex and fragment shaders into single `.glsl` files with inline type annotations. It also adds support for parsing and compiling these unified shader files in the OpenGL backend. Additionally, minor improvements were made to file handling and the sandbox layer.

### Shader System Refactor:
* **Unified Shader Files**: Combined vertex and fragment shaders into single `.glsl` files with `#type` annotations. For example, `Basic.vert` and `Basic.frag` were merged into `Basic.glsl` (`Assets/Shaders/Basic.vert` → `Assets/Shaders/Basic.glsl`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6dc874d160c94df097ed1811146e6c9d1b0d2fdfd46b61b50733e9096dbbf120R1) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6dc874d160c94df097ed1811146e6c9d1b0d2fdfd46b61b50733e9096dbbf120R19-R34).
* **Shader Parsing and Compilation**: Added `ParseShader` method in `OpenGLShader` to parse `#type` annotations and compile multiple shader stages from a single file. Introduced `ShaderTypeFromString` for type resolution (`Idra/src/Platform/OpenGL/OpenGLShader.cpp`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-24d0bb7b024b40f26e8eb1c8ca2f7130417a83fbed10fd70409011636a7233e2R10-R56) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-24d0bb7b024b40f26e8eb1c8ca2f7130417a83fbed10fd70409011636a7233e2L129-R207).
* **New Shader Constructor**: Added a constructor to `OpenGLShader` for handling unified `.glsl` files and updated `Shader::Create` to support this (`Idra/include/Platform/OpenGL/OpenGLShader.h`, `Idra/src/Renderer/Shader.cpp`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-16bf5fed9d5c8e33d8ebf6a7ef8be4417e0e49f3a9d63c79f24ae58ba030641dR8-L17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-70067682040e71d76f1aa6a05fafa48d2af6f6943c0d8850af48b7f062b40d2aR7-R27).

### Sandbox Layer Updates:
* **Shader Usage**: Updated `SandboxLayer` to use the new `.glsl` shader files instead of separate vertex and fragment files (`Editor/src/SandboxLayer.cpp`).
* **New Transform**: Added a second sphere transform (`m_Transform_Sphere2`) and integrated it into rendering (`Editor/include/SandboxLayer.h`, `Editor/src/SandboxLayer.cpp`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6f45d80fb4c8738e6a16e0c636bcc67098d95fc23a0119b8952a6afcd58b33baR53) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1ced46f15955f1d94f090a39911af64e03e613897494f8bdcc1af935213ace91R53) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-1ced46f15955f1d94f090a39911af64e03e613897494f8bdcc1af935213ace91R82-R83).

### Miscellaneous Improvements:
* **File Handling**: Renamed variables in `FileLoader` for clarity and consistency (`Idra/src/Resources/FileLoader.cpp`).
* **Code Cleanup**: Removed redundant `glAttachShader` calls in the old shader constructor (`Idra/src/Platform/OpenGL/OpenGLShader.cpp`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-24d0bb7b024b40f26e8eb1c8ca2f7130417a83fbed10fd70409011636a7233e2L24-L25) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-24d0bb7b024b40f26e8eb1c8ca2f7130417a83fbed10fd70409011636a7233e2R253).

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
# Fix latitude and longitude assignment in PlaceController

## 問題点
PlaceControllerの`create`メソッドで緯度と経度の値が逆に割り当てられていました。これにより、新しい場所を作成する際に座標が逆になり、マップピンが正しく配置されない問題が発生していました。特に日本の住所（番地以降）を入力した場合に、正確な場所に案内されないリスクがありました。

```typescript
// 修正前
const { name, address, location: { lat: longitude, lng: latitude } } = data;
```

## 変更内容
- PlaceControllerの`create`メソッドで緯度と経度の割り当てを修正
- `lat`の値を`latitude`（緯度）に、`lng`の値を`longitude`（経度）に正しく割り当て

```typescript
// 修正後
const { name, address, location: { lat: latitude, lng: longitude } } = data;
```

## 期待される効果
- 新しく作成される場所のマップピンが正しい位置に表示される
- 日本の住所（番地以降）を入力した場合でも、より正確な位置にピンが表示される

## 注意点
- 既存のデータについては、緯度と経度が逆になっている可能性があるため、必要に応じてデータの修正が検討されるべきです

Link to Devin run: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/6f114189c8454f129f9b429b335c8035

author: skx
body:
This pull-request is part of #234, making some improvements but not
yet resolving the issue.   It seems there are some issues with our
implementation which are not yet resolved however there are some
clear issues:

* We're missing some of the syscalls that the binaries call.
* We have issues handling the $-files, as created by SUBMIT.COM

I think we also don't reset FCB details when files are opened which leads to reading/writing to the wrong offsets if the caller doesn't pay attention.  (i.e. S1/CR/R0/R1/R2/Ex should be zero-filled when a file is made/opened, maybe?)

author: shapefuture
body:
This pull request implements the complete definitions for various types related to user profiles and cognitive skills in the MINDFRAME OS codebase. The following changes have been made:

1. **UserProfile**: Enhanced with detailed properties including user interests and proficiency levels.
2. **SJTScenarioOption**: Defined to represent answer options for Situational Judgment Tests, including cognitive bias targeting.
3. **SJTScenario**: Introduced to encapsulate a full scenario with options and bias explanations.
4. **CompletedChallenge**: Added to log entries for completed challenges, capturing relevant details.
5. **MindframeStoreState**: Expanded to include user profile, wisdom XP, and logs of completed challenges and drills.
6. **LLMInsight**: Defined for insights generated by the LLM, including cognitive patterns and related skills.
7. **OfflineInsight**: Similar to LLMInsight but with an optional CSS selector for highlighting.
8. **HCData**: Introduced to represent higher-order cognitive skills with unique identifiers and descriptions.

These changes eliminate all placeholders and provide a comprehensive structure for managing user profiles and cognitive skills, addressing the requirements outlined in the issue.

author: int128
body:
`oauth2.S256ChallengeOption` is available since oauth2 v0.13.0.
https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/oauth2@v0.30.0#S256ChallengeOption

## Breaking change ⚠️ 
Before:

```go
	pkce, err := oauth2params.NewPKCE()
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	cfg := oauth2cli.Config{
		AuthCodeOptions:      pkce.AuthCodeOptions(),
		TokenRequestOptions:  pkce.TokenRequestOptions(),
	}
```

After:

```go
	pkceVerifier := oauth2.GenerateVerifier()
	cfg := oauth2cli.Config{
		AuthCodeOptions:      []oauth2.AuthCodeOption{oauth2.S256ChallengeOption(pkceVerifier)},
		TokenRequestOptions:  []oauth2.AuthCodeOption{oauth2.VerifierOption(pkceVerifier)},
	}
```

author: pepongucte266
body:
Introduces `memory-bank/db.sql`, establishing the initial database schema for the application. This schema includes tables for `users` (linked to `auth.users`), `groups`, `group_members`, `expenses`, `expense_shares`, and `payments`. A PL/pgSQL trigger function is also defined to automatically manage `updated_at` timestamps across these tables. This structure provides the foundation for tracking shared expenses and financial settlements within groups.

Additionally, updates were made to the following Vue components:
- `src/components/ExcelImport.vue`
- `src/components/ListSaveAccount.vue`
- `src/components/ManualInputForm.vue`

These component changes likely adapt the UI to the new data model or enhance related expense input and management functionalities.

body: #### Description This pull request implements the core user authentication functionalities required for Sprint 2, including user login, registration with address handling, and logout. It establishes a robust authentication flow integrated with the CommerceTools API and sets up a foundation for managing user sessions and error handling. **Key accomplishments:** * **Authentication Service (`AuthService.ts`):** * Implemented methods for user `login` (using `/me/login` for cart merge and Password Flow for tokens), `register` (using `/me/signup` with anonymous session for cart merge), and `logout` (including token revocation). * Manages anonymous sessions (`AnonymousSessionService.ts`) for guest interactions and cart merging. * Handles token acquisition and in-memory storage for user sessions (to comply with RSS-ECOMM-2_07 "do not save" for this sprint). * Includes service-level data validation using Yup schemas before API calls. * **State Management (`authStore.ts`):** * Pinia store created to manage authentication state (`isUserLoggedIn`, `userProfile`, `isLoading`, `currentError`). * Provides actions (`signIn`, `signUp`, `signOut`, `initializeAuth`) coverage `AuthService` for operations. * Handles error states and integrates with `vue-toastification` for user notifications. * **Error Handling (`appErrors.ts`, `i18nKeys.ts`, locale files):** * Implemented a system of custom typed errors (`AuthError`, `ClientValidationError`, etc.) extending `AppError`. * `parseApiError` function processes errors from CommerceTools SDK and Yup. * Integrated `vue-i18n` for localized error messages and success notifications, displayed via toasts. * **API Client & Configuration (`ctpClient.ts`, `ctpClientBuilderFactory.ts`, `ctpConfig.ts`):** * Manages API client credentials and project settings retrieval. * **UI Integration:** * The developed services and store are fully integrated with the UI forms for login and registration. * **Project Settings:** * Implemented `ProjectSettingsService` and `projectSettingsStore` to dynamically fetch project configurations like available countries and languages from CommerceTools. **Covered Requirements:** * ✅ **RSS-ECOMM-2_03:** * ✅ **RSS-ECOMM-2_04:** * ✅ **RSS-ECOMM-2_07:** * ✅ **RSS-ECOMM-2_11:** * ✅ **RSS-ECOMM-2_12:** * ✅ **RSS-ECOMM-2_14:** * ✅ **RSS-ECOMM-2_15:** * ✅ **RSS-ECOMM-2_23:** #### Media (optional) #### Checklist - [x] 👀 I have performed a self-review of my code - [x] 💭 I have commented my code in areas that are hard to understand author: sichter
body:
During the preparation for the next upcoming commits it became obvious that the methods of the `Candidate` and `FPCandidate` classes which promote a successful candidate as featured picture would profit from some improvements to their docstrings.  The many steps of the parking procedure can easily be confused, therefore we can avoid misunderstandings and help future contributors if we make clear what is done by which method.

For the same purpose I have also renamed the local variables for the various variants of the gallery link that are used in `handlePassedCandidate()` and renamed the method `addToCategorizedFeaturedList()` to `addToGalleryPage()`.  The old name of that method was a leftover from the time when the systematic FP gallery pages were called ‘Categories’; this was quite confusing because they are just gallery pages, not categories as we have them on Commons today.  Therefore I propose to change that misleading method name, too, because the method has nothing to do with categories.

Let’s cancel the promotion process of a successful featured picture candidate (or set) as early as possible if the gallery page is not defined.

Describe your pull request here ---- Please read the [guidelines for Bioconda recipes](https://bioconda.github.io/contributor/guidelines.html) before opening a pull request (PR). ### General instructions * If this PR adds or updates a recipe, use "Add" or "Update" appropriately as the first word in its title. * New recipes not directly relevant to the biological sciences need to be submitted to the [conda-forge channel](https://conda-forge.org/docs/) instead of Bioconda. * PRs require reviews prior to being merged. Once your PR is passing tests and ready to be merged, please issue the `@BiocondaBot please add label` command. * Please post questions [on Gitter](https://gitter.im/bioconda/Lobby) or ping `@bioconda/core` in a comment. ### Instructions for avoiding API, ABI, and CLI breakage issues Conda is able to record and lock (a.k.a. pin) dependency versions used at build time of other recipes. This way, one can avoid that expectations of a downstream recipe with regards to API, ABI, or CLI are violated by later changes in the recipe. If not already present in the meta.yaml, make sure to specify `run_exports` (see [here](https://bioconda.github.io/contributor/linting.html#missing-run-exports) for the rationale and comprehensive explanation). Add a `run_exports` section like this: ```yaml build: run_exports: - ... ``` with `...` being one of: | Case | run_exports statement | | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | | semantic versioning | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x") }}` | | semantic versioning (0.x.x) | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x.x") }}` | | known breakage in minor versions | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x.x") }}` (in such a case, please add a note that shortly mentions your evidence for that) | | known breakage in patch versions | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x.x.x") }}` (in such a case, please add a note that shortly mentions your evidence for that) | | calendar versioning | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin=None) }}` | while replacing `"myrecipe"` with either `name` if a `name|lower` variable is defined in your recipe or with the lowercase name of the package in quotes. ### Bot commands for PR management
Please use the following BiocondaBot commands: Everyone has access to the following BiocondaBot commands, which can be given in a comment:
@BiocondaBot please update Merge the master branch into a PR.
@BiocondaBot please add label Add the please review & merge label.
@BiocondaBot please fetch artifacts Post links to CI-built packages/containers.
You can use this to test packages locally.
Note that the @BiocondaBot please merge command is now depreciated. Please just squash and merge instead. Also, the bot watches for comments from non-members that include `@bioconda/` and will automatically re-post them to notify the addressed ``.

Now Euler() Adams(4) instead of DPM(3) Euler()

While the total distortions aren't really any better on quickdif,

author: nyanpasu64
body:
#488 made corrscope check master audio for mono, then upmix it to stereo to prevent ffmpeg/video players from playing it at reduced volume. It used Python's wave module, which unfortunately does not support floating-point WAV files. This has been reported upstream at https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/60729, but unfortunately there appears to be no interest in fixing it.

~~This commit switches to using my vendored wavfile library. This doesn't support 24-bit integer samples, but we already reject those for channels.~~

~~If necessary I could introduce a cut-down WAV-probing library that *only* parses the "fmt " chunk and counts channels.~~

This PR adds a stripped-down wavfile library which probes and returns the WAV format, fixing support for floating-point samples *and* 24-bit integers.

Reported in #504.

author: chelyocarpus
body:
## Summary by Sourcery

Implement comprehensive mobile UX enhancements by introducing floating action buttons and slide-up panels for shelf addition and group management, refactor logger and util modules with robust fallbacks and new helpers, and improve table saving and rendering workflows with group date synchronization and dynamic row highlighting.

New Features:
- Add mobile FAB buttons for quick access to add-shelf and group-management panels.
- Implement slide-up mobile panels for adding shelves and viewing/editing groups with backdrop and keyboard-aware scrolling.
- Enhance custom alert dialogs into accessible modals with confirm/cancel support, custom styling, auto-close, and focus management.

Enhancements:
- Provide a default logger with leveled methods and setLogLevel, falling back to console when unavailable.
- Extend utils with waitForElement and scrollToElement functions and improve showAlert for modal behavior and touch-friendly styling.
- Normalize dates across linked shelves before saving, emit a beforeTableRender event, and use DataTable draw events to scroll and highlight updated rows.

## Overview
1. DB migration
2. Track active user (front-/backend/db)
3. UI adaptation
4. New APIs to delete matches/userstats
5. Direct winRate calculation

### re 1.
- implements new schema where the match table includes optionally the ids of player1 or 2, meaning:
- if player1Id is set (with the id of the active user at the time), it means the active user was player1
- if player2Id is set, the active user was player2
- if none is set, none of both players was the active user (is the case for tournament matches where some other players are playing)

### re 2.
- frontend:
- simple game - the first player is the active user
- tournament - active user can mark which of the player he chooses via a radio button
- adaptation of game mechanics to pass on active usernickname/role
- backend:
- adapts API chain to process active user and persist the appropriate data in the db

### re 3.
- single game: visual indication that player1 is the active user
- tournament: radio button to choose player for active user
- stats: indication which player was the active user in the matches table, new table to show if a match was part of a tournament (backend delivers tournament object when user matches are retrieved)

### re 4.
- adds API to delete all matches
- adds API to delete all userstats
-> required for testing of new tracking feature
- refactor of userstats folder/file structure: although we discussed previously to fuse userstats controllers & routes into the user files, I reintroduced those files to contain the functions which serve general requests which affect all matches/userstats (get/delete) in contrast to user specific requests for matches/userstats that pertain to the active user which still remains with the user files. Imo this aligns better with the existing structure where api chains that affect all matches/tournaments also have their independent files. A rework of the routes might be required as the user routes function a bit different than all the others. Can be discussed separately.

### re 5.
- calculates winRate directly in updateUserStats()
- somehow the middleware that was supposed to calculate winRate once the userstats are updated didn't work for me. Prisma middleware seems to not be very reliable as it has very specific requirements in order to work. Seems anyways to complicated for what can be solved with a few lines in updateUserStats(). Can also be discussed.

author: anandamideshakyan
body:
## Description
Addresses https://github.com/prestodb/presto/issues/25104 
Currently, Presto does not support INSERT INTO operations on bucketed but unpartitioned Hive tables. This limitation originates from a hard check in HiveWriterFactory:

https://github.com/prestodb/presto/blob/master/presto-hive/src/main/java/com/facebook/presto/hive/HiveWriterFactory.java#L480

## Motivation and Context

Supporting writes to bucketed unpartitioned Hive tables in Presto would improve compatibility and enhance Presto’s ability to handle modern Hive table layouts. It's a reasonable and useful feature for users who wish to leverage bucketing for performance optimizations even without partitioning.

## Impact

This change would align Presto’s behavior with the broader SQL-on-Hadoop ecosystem and remove an artificial limitation that may block valid use cases — particularly in data warehousing environments where bucketing is used independently of partitioning.

## Release Notes
```
== RELEASE NOTES ==

Hive Connector Changes

* Add support for INSERT into bucketed but unpartitioned Hive tables in Hive, including follow-up fixes for native validation and insert handling.

```

author: kerthcet
body:
**Commit Message**

This commit added new fields CreatedAt & OwnedBy to AIGatewayRoute as well as the internal Backend, so people can customize the output of OpenAI-compatible APIs. 

We set the fields at `AIGatewayRouteRule` level, the main two reasons here:

- I believe for most of the cases, we only match one model at the `Matches` fields, so working at `AIGatewayRouteRule` seems not bad as the model:modelOwner = 1:1
- for different backends, the modelOwner:backends = 1:n, because backends just means different route paths for one model, so working at `AIGatewayRouteRule` level also makes sense.

One shortcoming here is in fallover mode, like we set different backends for one model service, e.g. Envoy AI Gateway + openai, then we will have the same modelOwner for them, it's a bit confusing. 

But I persist on this just because when querying the `/models` list, let's assume that we'll have two models sharing the same modelOwner (different with the current implementation):

- even the enduser gets two models, but actually they can not select which backend to query, the only knob for them is the model name

**Subsystem**
Server, Configuration

**Motivation**
- [KTOR-8436](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KTOR-8436) Config deserialisation not respecting testApplication environment
- [KTOR-8517](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KTOR-8517) File configuration loading test API short-hand

**Solution**
Added support for config value deserialization for both `MapApplicationConfig` and `MergedApplicationConfig`.  Now you can combine any number of configuration sources and deserialize properties.

I've also introduced a short-hand for the test application context for configuring from files.  Instead of `environment { config = ApplicationConfig("file.conf") }` you can call `configure("file.conf")`.  This accepts a variable number of string args and merges all config files loaded this way.

  Hermetic CUDA uses a specific downloadable version of CUDA instead of the user’s locally installed CUDA. Bazel will download CUDA, CUDNN and NCCL distributions, and then use CUDA libraries and tools as dependencies in various Bazel targets. author: st0012
body:
[Feature #15854](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/15854)

This PR introduces:

- A new `ivar_set` event to `TracePoint`, which will be triggered when a instance variable is set through:
    - Direct assignment, like `@a = 1`
    - Attribute setters, like `Foo.a = 1`
    - `instance_variable_set`
- A new `ivar_name` method to `TracePoint` instances that's only available for this event to retrieve the ivar's name in Symbol
    - The value can be retrieved through `TracePoint#return_value`

### Example

```rb
TracePoint.trace(:ivar_set) do |tp|
  puts "ivar_set: #{tp.ivar_name.inspect}, value: #{tp.return_value.inspect}"
end

class Foo
  attr_accessor :b

  def initialize
    @a = 1
  end
end

foo = Foo.new
foo.b = 2
foo.instance_variable_set(:@c, 3)
# ivar_set: :@a, value: 1, lineno: 9
# ivar_set: :@b, value: 2, lineno: 14
# ivar_set: :@c, value: 3, lineno: 15
```

body:
This is part of the process in making this repo easy to contribute to in order to attract contributors.

The linting results are completely different, depending whether you run `yarn react:dev`or `yarn lint`. This is because craco uses a very simple internal eslint config.

Craco does not support the eslint flat config, so there is currently no way to point it at the config.

The best solution appears to be to disable craco's linting and create two sets of rules, one for the main process and one for the renderer process.

The rules I have chosen are a fairly common set for Electron Typescript React projects.

Of course, you may disagree with the rules I have chosen; just let me know... your project, your rules.

As part of this process I have also added a `.prettierrc` because eslint needs this in order for its Prettier plugins to work.

author: mikeratcliffe
body:
This is part of the process in making this repo easy to contribute to in order to attract contributors.

The linting results are completely different, depending whether you run `yarn react:dev`or `yarn lint`. This is because craco uses a very simple internal eslint config.

Craco does not support the eslint flat config, so there is currently no way to point it at the config.

The best solution appears to be to disable craco's linting and create two sets of rules, one for the main process and one for the renderer process.

The rules I have chosen are a fairly common set for Electron Typescript React projects.

Of course, you may disagree with the rules I have chosen; just let me know... your project, your rules.

As part of this process I have also added a `.prettierrc` because eslint needs this in order for its Prettier plugins to work.

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [commander](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js) | dependencies | major | [`^12.1.0` -> `^14.0.0`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/commander/12.1.0/14.0.0) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>tj/commander.js (commander)</summary>

### [`v14.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1400-2025-05-18)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/compare/v13.1.0...v14.0.0)

##### Added

-   support for groups of options and commands in the help using low-level `.helpGroup()` on `Option` and `Command`, and higher-level `.optionsGroup()` and `.commandsGroup()` which can be used in chaining way to specify group title for following options/commands (\[[#​2328](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2328)])
-   support for unescaped negative numbers as option-arguments and command-arguments (\[[#​2339](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2339)])
-   TypeScript: add `parseArg` property to `Argument` class (\[[#​2359](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2359)])

##### Fixed

-   remove bogus leading space in help when option has default value but not a description (\[[#​2348](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2348)])
-   `.configureOutput()` now makes copy of settings instead of modifying in-place, fixing side-effects (\[[#​2350](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2350)])

##### Changed

-   *Breaking:* Commander 14 requires Node.js v20 or higher
-   internal refactor of `Help` class adding `.formatItemList()` and `.groupItems()` methods (\[[#​2328](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2328)])

### [`v13.1.0`](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1310-2025-01-21)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/compare/v13.0.0...v13.1.0)

##### Added

-   support a pair of long option flags to allow a memorable shortened flag, like `.option('--ws, --workspace')` (\[[#​2312](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2312)])

### [`v13.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1300-2024-12-30)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/compare/v12.1.0...v13.0.0)

##### Added

-   support multiple calls to `.parse()` with default settings (\[[#​2299](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2299)])
-   add `.saveStateBeforeParse()` and `.restoreStateBeforeParse()` for use by subclasses (\[[#​2299](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2299)])
-   style routines like `styleTitle()` to add color to help using `.configureHelp()` or Help subclass (\[[#​2251](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2251)])
-   color related support in `.configureOutput()` for `getOutHasColors()`, `getErrHasColors()`, and `stripColor()` (\[[#​2251](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2251)])
-   Help property for `minWidthToWrap` (\[[#​2251](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2251)])
-   Help methods for `displayWidth()`, `boxWrap()`, `preformatted()` et al (\[[#​2251](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2251)])

##### Changed

-   *Breaking*: excess command-arguments cause an error by default, see migration tips (\[[#​2223](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2223)])
-   *Breaking*: throw during Option construction for unsupported option flags, like multiple characters after single `-` (\[[#​2270](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2270)])
    -   note: support for dual long option flags added in Commander 13.1
-   *Breaking*: throw on multiple calls to `.parse()` if `storeOptionsAsProperties: true` (\[[#​2299](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2299)])
-   TypeScript: include implicit `this` in parameters for action handler callback (\[[#​2197](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2197)])

##### Deleted

-   *Breaking*: `Help.wrap()` refactored into `formatItem()` and `boxWrap()` (\[[#​2251](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2251)])

##### Migration Tips

**Excess command-arguments**

It is now an error for the user to specify more command-arguments than are expected. (`allowExcessArguments` is now false by default.)

Old code:

```js
program.option('-p, --port <number>', 'port number');
program.action((options) => {
  console.log(program.args);
});
```

Now shows an error:

```console
$ node example.js a b c
error: too many arguments. Expected 0 arguments but got 3.
```

You can declare the expected arguments. The help will then be more accurate too. Note that declaring
new arguments will change what is passed to the action handler.

```js
program.option('-p, --port <number>', 'port number');
program.argument('[args...]', 'remote command and arguments'); // expecting zero or more arguments
program.action((args, options) => {
  console.log(args);
});
```

Or you could suppress the error, useful for minimising changes in legacy code.

```js
program.option('-p, --port', 'port number');
program.allowExcessArguments();
program.action((options) => {
  console.log(program.args);
});
```

**Stricter option flag parsing**

Commander now throws an error for option flag combinations that are not supported.
In particular, a short flag with multiple characters is now an error.

```js
program.option('-ws, --workspace'); // throws error
```

A short option has a single character:

```js
program.option('-w, --workspace');
```

Or from Commander 13.1 you can have an extra long flag instead of a short flag to allow a more memorable shortcut for the full name:

```js
program.option('--ws, --workspace');
```

</details>

body:
This pull request introduces significant enhancements to the estimation functionality for blockchain operations in the `core-js` package. The changes include new API methods for estimating various types of transactions, the addition of comprehensive type definitions, and the implementation of a utility function for estimating Aptos raw transactions.

### API Enhancements:
* Replaced the deprecated `estimateOrder` method with specialized methods for estimating different blockchain operations, such as token transfers, NFT transfers, raw transactions (EVM and Aptos), NFT minting, and NFT collection creation. These methods include error handling and validation for missing or invalid response data. (`[packages/core-js/src/api/bff.tsL203-R371](diffhunk://#diff-8c5d54af109bc893c2a7d6a6d502adf039961d3327300553a42edda790203241L203-R371)`)

### Type Definitions:
* Added new type definitions in `bff/estimate.ts` to support the new estimation methods, including request and response structures for token transfers, NFT transfers, raw transactions, NFT minting, and NFT collection creation. These types ensure type safety and clarity when interacting with the estimation API. (`[packages/core-js/src/types/bff/estimate.tsR1-R270](diffhunk://#diff-a083eca472a4c694d91f07d3785fb7672a2f0d8dacaf7d6acd53b3b09626f835R1-R270)`)

### Utility Function:
* Implemented the `estimateAptosRawTransaction` function to generate Aptos raw transaction estimates. This function validates input, constructs the required request body, and processes the response to return a user operation and transaction details. (`[packages/core-js/src/userop/estimateAptosRawTransaction.tsR1-R197](diffhunk://#diff-1a0bcfc1dce880467dfed6af69234ebc501b3790d1423781da5dc2f26e08630bR1-R197)`)

### Codebase Refactoring:
* Updated imports in `bff.ts` to include the new type definitions and removed unused imports for deprecated functionality. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8c5d54af109bc893c2a7d6a6d502adf039961d3327300553a42edda790203241L5-L7)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8c5d54af109bc893c2a7d6a6d502adf039961d3327300553a42edda790203241R16-R29)`)
* Exported the new `estimate.ts` types in `bff/index.ts` to make them accessible throughout the codebase. (`[packages/core-js/src/types/bff/index.tsR5](diffhunk://#diff-6bcd9f2dd80dd06c7438d58e5340e09a5b0a553aff8c81f6966fb00990423293R5)`)

# Fix get_buf_diff to use user config settings

## Problem
The `get_buf_diff` function was using default configuration settings from `config.lua` directly, rather than using the user-configured settings from `init.vim`. This meant that any custom settings specified by users in their `init.vim` were not being applied to the diff calculation logic.

## Solution
1. Moved the `get_buf_diff` function from `init.lua` to `buffer.lua` to improve code modularity
2. Implemented an `update_config` function in the buffer module to receive updated configuration
3. Updated the `setup` function in `init.lua` to call `buffer.update_config(config)` after merging user settings
4. Updated all references to `get_buf_diff` in `init.lua` to use the buffer module's version

## Testing
The changes have been manually verified by code inspection to ensure that:
- The buffer module receives the merged configuration that includes user settings
- All references to `get_buf_diff` have been updated to use the buffer module's version
- The function signature and behavior remain the same, only the configuration source has changed

author: rozsazoltan
body:
Fixes #3885 

I believe the `3.75rem` min-height was set for safety reasons. However, this makes it impractical to use smaller font sizes, such as the default `text-xs`, and requires strong overrides.

The `1lh` value is supported by all browsers targeted as the minimum by TailwindCSS v4. Since DaisyUI also relies on TailwindCSS v4, I believe using `1lh` is justified. Moreover, if it's not supported, the fallback value of `3.75rem` still works well.

author: arnaudbarre
body:
The current HMR implementation was trying to all HMR files that contains either hooks or components, but this was working only for components and lead to HMR invalidation for JSX files containing hooks.

The best solution would have been to support HMR for hooks, but in my testing it was sometimes leading to stale updates. So this simple and reliable solution is to skip HMR for these files and have the components handle the updates, like any other hooks file.

Fixes #289
Fixes #354
Fixes #411

    - 게시글 목록을 가져오는 커스텀 훅이 도입되어 데이터 조회가 간편해졌습니다.

author: svalanukonda
body:
his PR fixes an issue where watch client notifications were incorrectly triggered for GET commands.

The solution introduces a new function, IsNotifiableCmd, to control when notifications should be triggered. This ensures that:
1.Notifications are triggered only for Data Manipulation (DM) operations, not for Data Read (DR) operations.
2. An exception list (implemented as a hash map) allows fine-grained control over notification triggers for specific commands.

- Registrar registration and management
- NFT property deed registration and transfer capabilities
- Jurisdiction validation with assessment values
- Property attribute management
- Comprehensive read-only functions for data access

The implementation follows Clarity best practices and passes all Clarinet checks without errors or warnings. The contract allows authorized registrars to create digital property deeds as NFTs, jurisdictions to validate properties with assessment values, and owners to transfer these deeds securely, creating a robust decentralized property registry system.

# Support for long-running processes in executeCommand tool

## Description
This PR addresses [Issue #21](https://github.com/aws-samples/remote-swe-agents/issues/21) by adding support for daemon-like processes (e.g., `npm run dev` or `docker compose up`) in the executeCommand tool.

## Changes
- Added a new property `longRunningProcess: boolean` to the existing `executeCommand` tool
- When `longRunningProcess: true`, the tool does not wait for the process to exit; instead, it leaves the process running in the background
- The tool waits for 10 seconds before returning control to allow for process initialization
- Any output generated during those 10 seconds is captured and returned to the agent
- If the process fails within the 10-second initialization period, an error is returned

## Tests
- Built successfully with `npm run build`

## Additional Notes
- This enables the agent to start development servers and other daemon processes that would otherwise time out
- Users need to explicitly set `longRunningProcess: true` to activate this behavior

body:
## Description
This PR adds support for boolean type conversion in the JasyncRow class. Previously, the class supported conversions for various data types but did not explicitly handle boolean values. With these changes, the class can now properly convert various input data types (Numbers, Strings, Booleans) to Boolean values.

This enhancement is particularly important for MySQL databases, which represent boolean values as TINYINT(1) where 0 means false and any non-zero value (typically 1) means true. Our implementation correctly handles this MySQL-specific behavior by treating any non-zero numeric value as true.

## Changes Made
- Extended the get method in JasyncRow to handle boolean conversions with the following mapping:
  - Numbers: 0 → false, non-zero → true (aligned with MySQL's TINYINT(1) representation of booleans)
  - Strings: Using Kotlin's built-in Boolean parsing
  - Boolean values: Preserved as-is
  - Added proper handling for primitive boolean type
- Added comprehensive test cases in JasyncRowTest to validate all conversion scenarios
## Testing
- Created a dedicated test class JasyncRowTest with a test method testBooleanConversion that verifies:
  - Boolean to Boolean conversion
  - Number to Boolean conversion (0 → false, non-zero → true)
  - String to Boolean conversion ("true" → true, "false" → false)
  - Accessing Boolean values by index
  - Tests pass successfully, confirming the implementation works as expected

## Related Issue
https://github.com/jasync-sql/jasync-sql/issues/430

## Additional Notes
This change enables more flexible type handling in the database access layer, making it easier to work with boolean values returned from MySQL queries. Since MySQL stores boolean values as TINYINT(1), this implementation ensures a seamless conversion between the database representation and the application-level Boolean type, improving type safety and code readability.

author: ericndungutse
body:
## Description

This pull request introduces a new feature to display task details in the NovaTech Task Manager application. It includes the addition of a new servlet to handle task detail requests, a new JSP view for displaying task details, and an update to the task list view to include a "Details" button. Below are the most important changes:

### Backend Changes:
* **New servlet for task details:** Added `TaskDetailsServlet` to handle requests for viewing task details. It retrieves task information from the `TaskService` and forwards it to the new JSP view.

### Frontend Changes:
* **New task details view:** Created `task-details.jsp` to display detailed information about a task, including title, description, due date, and status. The view also includes buttons for editing, deleting, and navigating back to the task list.
* **Updated task list view:** Added a "Details" button to each task in `tasks.jsp`, linking to the task details page.

For newer version of dnf (dnf 5+) the `groupinstall` command no longer works. This is because the `groupinstall` was actually an alias to `group install` which was last supported until dnf4. So for newer versions of fedora, running the old command would throw an error saying `groupinstall` was not recognized as a command.

I have updated the following:
- `README.md`
- `docs/fedora.md`
---
This PR partially solves the issue #1001, since the wiki is still yet to be updated.

This should result in less errors like:

### [`v15.5.0`](https://redirect.github.com/lint-staged/lint-staged/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1550)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/lint-staged/lint-staged/compare/v15.4.3...v15.5.0)

##### Minor Changes

- [#​1526](https://redirect.github.com/lint-staged/lint-staged/pull/1526) [`630af5f`](https://redirect.github.com/lint-staged/lint-staged/commit/630af5fb48ed43eb6ccaefa7a9d9612309023b6f) Thanks [@​iiroj](https://redirect.github.com/iiroj)! - Lint-staged no longer resets to the original state when preventing an empty git commit. This happens when your configured tasks reset all the staged changes, typically when trying to commit formatting changes which conflict with your linter setup like ESLint or Prettier.

##### Example with Prettier

By default Prettier [prefers double quotes](https://prettier.io/docs/rationale#strings).

##### Previously

1. Stage `file.js` with only double quotes `"` changed to `'`
2. Run `git commit -am "I don't like double quotes"`
3. *Lint-staged* runs `prettier --write file.js`, converting all the `'` back to `"`
4. Because there are now no changes, *lint-staged* fails, cancels the commit, and resets back to the original state
5. Commit was not done, original state is restored and single quotes `'` are staged

##### Now

1. Stage `file.js` with only double-quotes `"` changed to `'`
2. Run `git commit -am "I don't like double quotes"`
3. *Lint-staged* runs `prettier --write file.js`, converting all the `'` back to `"`
4. Because there are now no changes, *lint-staged* fails and cancels the commit
5. Commit was not done, and there are no staged changes

##### Flow: Fix missing parentheses in `ConditionalTypeAnnotation` ([#​17196](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/pull/17196) by [@​fisker](https://redirect.github.com/fisker))

<!-- prettier-ignore -->

```jsx
// Input
type T<U> = 'a' | ('b' extends U ? 'c' : empty);
type T<U> = 'a' & ('b' extends U ? 'c' : empty);

// Prettier 3.5.2
type T<U> = "a" | "b" extends U ? "c" : empty;
type T<U> = "a" & "b" extends U ? "c" : empty;

// Prettier 3.5.3
type T<U> = "a" | ("b" extends U ? "c" : empty);

```

### [`v3.5.2`](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#352)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/compare/3.5.1...3.5.2)

##### Remove `module-sync` condition ([#​17156](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/pull/17156) by [@​fisker](https://redirect.github.com/fisker))

In Prettier 3.5.0, [we added `module-sync` condition to `package.json`](https://prettier.io/blog/2025/02/09/3.5.0#use-esm-entrypoint-for-requireesm-16958-by-tats-u), so that `require("prettier")` can use ESM version, but turns out it doesn't work if CommonJS and ESM plugins both imports builtin plugins. To solve this problem, we decide simply remove the `module-sync` condition, so `require("prettier")` will still use the CommonJS version, we'll revisit until `require(ESM)` feature is more stable.

### [`v3.5.1`](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#351)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/compare/3.5.0...3.5.1)

[diff](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/compare/3.5.0...3.5.1)

##### Fix CLI crash when cache for old version exists ([#​17100](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/pull/17100) by [@​sosukesuzuki](https://redirect.github.com/sosukesuzuki))

Prettier 3.5 uses a different cache format than previous versions, Prettier 3.5.0 crashes when reading existing cache file, Prettier 3.5.1 fixed the problem.

##### Support dockercompose and github-actions-workflow in VSCode ([#​17101](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/pull/17101) by [@​remcohaszing](https://redirect.github.com/remcohaszing))

## 📝 Summary

## 🔍 Description of Changes

## Tests

- Wrote small unit tests for unique transform handler using all 4 `keep` options.

body: Currently, the MCP Tool autoconfiguration defines the `SyncMcpToolCallbackProvider` and `AsyncMcpToolCallbackProvider` beans returning the `ToolCallbackProvider` interface. That generates autowiring warnings in IDEs when trying to inject the specific class. The Spring Boot project recommends being specific: > When declaring a @Bean method, provide as much type information as possible in the method’s return type. For example, if your bean’s concrete class implements an interface the bean method’s return type should be the concrete class and not the interface. Providing as much type information as possible in @Bean methods is particularly important when using bean conditions as their evaluation can only rely upon to type information that is available in the method signature. See https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/reference/features/developing-auto-configuration.html#features.developing-auto-configuration.condition-annotations.bean-conditions This PR ensures concrete classes are used. That's also in line with what included in the [documentation](https://docs.spring.io/spring-ai/reference/api/mcp/mcp-client-boot-starter-docs.html#_usage_example):

body:
# 🔮 Bitcoin Time Series Forecasting with SageMath

## 📌 Project Overview

This project focuses on **real-time Bitcoin price analysis and forecasting** using SageMath. The goal is to build a **fully reproducible pipeline** that:
- Ingests live Bitcoin data via API
- Preprocesses and cleans the data
- Performs exploratory data analysis (EDA)
- Applies multiple **forecasting models** including symbolic regression, ARIMA, and SARIMA
- Visualizes and reports insights

It serves as a demonstration of how **SageMath's symbolic and numerical computation power** can be harnessed for time series forecasting tasks in finance.

---

## 🔧 Key Components

### ✅ 1. Data Ingestion
- Python scripts fetch data from the CoinGecko API (`update_live_price.py`)
- Historical data is merged and cleaned using `pandas` and `csv` modules
- Stored locally in CSV for traceability and reproducibility

### ✅ 2. Data Preprocessing
- Handled in Sage notebooks using `pandas` for structure and `SymPy` for symbolic operations
- Missing timestamps filled
- Data smoothed using moving averages and rolling statistics

### ✅ 3. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
- Plots generated using `matplotlib` and `SageMath`'s built-in plotting utilities
- Visualizations include:
  - Full time series
  - Zoomed recent views
  - Histogram of prices
  - Volatility via rolling stddev

---

## 🔮 Forecasting Models in SageMath

### 📌 Symbolic Forecasting (SymPy in Sage)
- Polynomial models (degree 5 to 7) were fitted symbolically
- Enabled interpretable formulas
- Used to forecast future prices with human-readable expressions
- Sage's symbolic capabilities allowed manipulation and simplification of expressions, and even symbolic derivation for trend/inflection analysis

### 📌 ARIMA Forecasting
- Classical ARIMA model fitted to the cleaned time series
- Used Sage to:
- Construct models with specified (p,d,q) parameters
- Compare residuals
- Export ARIMA forecasts for visual evaluation

### 📌 SARIMA Forecasting
- Seasonal extension of ARIMA implemented to capture weekly/monthly cycles
- Used grid search within Sage to optimize seasonal parameters
- Forecast accuracy measured and residuals visualized

---

## 📊 Reporting and Visualization

- Forecast plots and comparison charts exported to `reports/`:
- `arima_vs_sarima_comparison.png`
- `symbolic_polynomial_fit.png`
- `final_plot.png` (combined view)
- Forecast data saved in CSVs like:

## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @UlisesGascon. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @UlisesGascon on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Least Privileged GitHub Actions Token Permissions

The GITHUB_TOKEN is an automatically generated secret to make authenticated calls to the GitHub API. GitHub recommends setting minimum token permissions for the GITHUB_TOKEN.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#using-the-github_token-in-a-workflow)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#token-permissions)
### Pinned Dependencies

GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to full length commit.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Detect Vulnerabilities with SAST Workflow 

Static Code Analysis (also known as Source Code Analysis) is usually performed as part of a Code Review (also known as clear-box testing) and is carried out at the Implementation phase of a Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#sast)
- [OWASP Static Code Analysis](https://owasp.org/www-community/controls/Static_Code_Analysis)

body:
This pull request introduces functionality for uploading files to an AWS S3 bucket and refactors the backend to support this feature. It also includes frontend updates to enable users to upload images from the UI. Below are the key changes grouped by theme:

### Frontend Enhancements
* Updated the `dev` script in `app/package.json` to allow specifying a custom port (`--port 5173`) during development.
* Added a file upload button in `GroupExpensesCard` within `app/src/app/dashboard/group/[id]/page.tsx`, enabling users to upload images. The button uses the new `handleFileUpload` function and displays success or error messages via `toast`. ([app/src/app/dashboard/group/[id]/page.tsxR216-R236](diffhunk://#diff-4dfe4891e843d5bf3ea9a3f1eebb102d8237b10f8a51f7483f01a6df8acdb722R216-R236))
* Imported the `handleFileUpload` function in `app/src/app/dashboard/group/[id]/page.tsx` to handle file uploads. ([app/src/app/dashboard/group/[id]/page.tsxR23](diffhunk://#diff-4dfe4891e843d5bf3ea9a3f1eebb102d8237b10f8a51f7483f01a6df8acdb722R23))

### Backend Enhancements
* Added a new `handleFileUpload` function in `app/src/client/user.ts` to send files to the backend using `axios`. This function uploads files as `multipart/form-data` to the `/upload/parse-invoice` endpoint.
* Introduced an `uploadToS3` service in `backend/services/uploadToS3.js` to handle file uploads to an AWS S3 bucket. This service reads the file, generates an S3 key using a UUID, and uploads the file to the `splitmate-jobs` bucket.

### Backend Refactoring
* Updated `backend/routes/api/fileUploadRoutes.js` to use the `uploadToS3` service. The route now uploads files to S3 instead of processing them with AWS Textract. The Textract-related code has been commented out for potential future use.
* Added dependencies for AWS SDK (`aws-sdk`) and UUID generation (`uuid`) in `backend/package.json` to support S3 uploads and unique job IDs.

These changes collectively enhance the application's file handling capabilities by integrating AWS S3 for secure and scalable file storage while improving the user experience with a seamless file upload process.

author: fawazadejo
body:
## Overview
This PR implements a simplified version of a decentralized financial fraud detection system using Clarity smart contracts. The system consists of five main contracts that work together to verify institutions, monitor transactions, score risk, manage alerts, and track investigations.

## Contracts Implemented

1. **Institution Verification Contract**
   - Validates financial entities in the system
   - Maintains a map of verified institutions
   - Provides functions to verify, check verification status, and revoke verification

2. **Transaction Monitoring Contract**
   - Records and stores transaction data
   - Provides functions to record transactions and retrieve transaction details

3. **Risk Scoring Contract**
   - Assigns risk scores to accounts
   - Provides functions to set risk scores, get risk scores, and check if an account is high risk

4. **Alert Management Contract**
   - Creates and manages alerts for potentially fraudulent activity
   - Provides functions to create alerts, resolve alerts, and retrieve alert details

5. **Investigation Tracking Contract**
   - Tracks the investigation process for fraud cases
   - Provides functions to create investigations, update investigation status, and retrieve investigation details

## Testing
- Tests are implemented using Vitest
- Tests cover basic functionality of all contracts
- Mock blockchain functions are used to simulate contract interactions

## Security Considerations
- Admin-only functions are protected with principal checks
- Data validation is performed before storage
- Error codes are used for clear error handling

## Future Improvements
- Add more sophisticated risk scoring algorithms
- Implement cross-contract calls for integrated functionality
- Add event emission for important state changes
- Enhance access control with multi-signature requirements
```

author: lucfd
body:
Fixed an issue where the parser would not properly copy the description of a few spells with unusually long descriptions (such as Hex, Wish, Summon Undead). These spells are formatted slightly differently, with their descriptions being broken up into multiple \

tags. `parse_to_json()` now concatenates all of these rather than just taking the value of the last one. `clean_list()` has been modified to remove any item that is not a `Spell` rather than just removing `None` from the list. Additionally, the method now removes duplicate spell entries, a few of which exist on the site due to UA spells being reprinted into source books with no changes (ex. Draconic Transformation, Antagonize, Spray of Cards).

body:
### What
This PR refactors the Renault Zoe implementation

### Why
This implementation is used by many different Renault vehicles, (Zoe 22/41 , Kangoo 33, Fluence ZE 22/36) , and it is a bit unclear what is sent by what generation of vehicle. This PR aims to make further improvements to the integration easier

### How

- We remove the calculated min/max cellvoltage lookups, and instead use the values sent constantly via CAN
- We add comments on those CAN messages that we are sure is sent by a specific model
- More Battery Info page added for the Zoe integration, so we can look at diagnostic data in more detail

2. Added support for both JSON and plain text formats with appropriate MIME types
3. Implemented resource change notifications when buffer content or cursor position changes
4. Preserved the enhanced buffer rendering with line numbers and cursor indication

6. Updated documentation with resource usage examples

This change improves integration with Claude and other LLM clients by following the MCP resource pattern where editor state is modeled as a resource rather than a tool action. The implementation also adds resource change notifications to keep clients updated when buffers change.
